<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518916062_theRebbe_542" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518916062_theRebbe_542__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the distinction between lights and vessels to resolve how change and the ten Sefiros can be attributed to the simple, unchanging Ein Sof.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood by prefacing the discourse of the master of joy and redemption,</t>
    <t s="2">the discourse "L'havin"</t>
    <t s="3">the matter of what is said in the Etz Chaim at its beginning, that the aspect of</t>
    <t s="4">the Nekudim are ten lights in ten vessels,</t>
    <t s="5">and the aspect of the Akudim [is that] all</t>
    <t s="6">(ten)</t>
    <t s="7">the lights are bound in one vessel,</t>
    <t s="8">and he explains,</t>
    <t s="9">that to understand this, one must first preface to understand how the matter of ten Sefiros,</t>
    <t s="10">Chochmah and Binah etc., can apply Above in Ein Sof,</t>
    <t s="11">for the name Chochmah and Binah etc. indicates that it is an aspect of the existence of some thing in some essence,</t>
    <t s="12">whereas Ein Sof is a simple light,</t>
    <t s="13">to the extent that even the world of Atzilus is in the aspect of Bli Mah.</t>
    <t s="14">And similarly regarding the aspect of Kesser, which is called Ratzon,</t>
    <t s="15">which is above the ten Sefiros,</t>
    <t s="16">and like in the powers of the soul,</t>
    <t s="17">that the power of will is above all the internal powers,</t>
    <t s="18">to the extent that it is explained in many places</t>
    <t s="19">that will is not a separate entity from the soul like Chochmah and what is below it,</t>
    <t s="20">for the entire matter of will is that it effects a matter of change,</t>
    <t s="21">as they say "Yehi Ratzon",</t>
    <t s="22">which means a new will,</t>
    <t s="23">that is, that it changes from how it was beforehand,</t>
    <t s="24">and it follows,</t>
    <t s="25">that there is a change between before He wills,</t>
    <t s="26">at the time He wills,</t>
    <t s="27">and after He wills,</t>
    <t s="28">and it is impossible to say in any way that an aspect of change exists Above,</t>
    <t s="29">for it is said of Him,</t>
    <t s="30">"I, Hashem, have not changed."</t>
    <t s="31">And the point of the explanation of this is the distinction between lights and vessels,</t>
    <t s="32">that from the perspective of the vessels there is the matter of the ten Sefiros,</t>
    <t s="33">to the extent that they are called by the names Chochmah and Binah etc.,</t>
    <t s="34">and likewise the matter of will which is above that,</t>
    <t s="35">but from the perspective of the lights it is in a manner of simplicity, of the simple unity that is above all these matters,</t>
    <t s="36">and about this it is said, "I, Hashem, have not changed."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section uses the analogy of the human soul to explain the distinction between concealment and revelation, showing that change only arises from the vessels, not from the essence of the soul.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And it will be understood from what is seen in man below,</t>
    <t s="2">"From my flesh I shall perceive G-d",</t>
    <t s="3">that there is a distinction between concealment and revelation.</t>
    <t s="4">For behold,</t>
    <t s="5">all the matters that exist in man in revelation,</t>
    <t s="6">the possibility of their revelation is because they exist beforehand in concealment in his soul.</t>
    <t s="7">And like Chochmah, which is the first of the internal powers,</t>
    <t s="8">behold, its revelation in man is by virtue of it existing beforehand in the essence of his soul,</t>
    <t s="9">except that in the essence of his soul it is not in a manner of revealed Chochmah that can be grasped in the vessel of understanding and comprehension of Binah,</t>
    <t s="10">rather there it is only a hylic potential,</t>
    <t s="11">from which the matter of Chochmah and intellect can later come.</t>
    <t s="12">And even as it later comes to revelation,</t>
    <t s="13">behold, it is in a manner that first the power of the intellect is drawn,</t>
    <t s="14">in which the matter of comprehension and grasp through the vessel of Binah does not yet apply,</t>
    <t s="15">as it is the power of the intellect over all types of intellect and Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="16">and afterwards from the power of the intellect there is also drawn a matter of revealed Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="17">a specific Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="18">which can then come into the palace of Binah,</t>
    <t s="19">"a point in the palace".</t>
    <t s="20">And behold,</t>
    <t s="21">as the powers are in the essence of the soul, then it is not possible to distinguish between one power and another,</t>
    <t s="22">for the soul is simple,</t>
    <t s="23">and likewise the matter of changes does not apply there,</t>
    <t s="24">as they are there in simplicity,</t>
    <t s="25">and they are only a source from which can later be drawn</t>
    <t s="26">(regarding the matter of intellect)</t>
    <t s="27">the power of the intellect and afterwards intellect and revealed Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="28">and therefore it is called by the name Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="29">because it is a source for Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="30">but the entire matter of Chochmah and intellect exists there in a manner of concealment,</t>
    <t s="31">and it is also called by the name "light".</t>
    <t s="32">However,</t>
    <t s="33">when it is later drawn in revelation,</t>
    <t s="34">behold, this is through the matter of vessels,</t>
    <t s="35">and from the perspective of the matter of vessels, a matter of change occurs,</t>
    <t s="36">that there is one in whom the power of the intellect etc. influences many matters of Chochmah, in multiplicity both in quantity and in quality,</t>
    <t s="37">and there is one in whom the revelation does not come in such multiplicity nor in these wisdoms,</t>
    <t s="38">with many differences between one and another.</t>
    <t s="39">And all the more so when it is drawn into revealed Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="40">then there is a greater difference between one and another,</t>
    <t s="41">to the extent that even in this same person there are changes from time to time,</t>
    <t s="42">and this is,</t>
    <t s="43">that in addition to the general change that "with many years they make wisdom known",</t>
    <t s="44">there is also a change from time to time in this same year and in this same day,</t>
    <t s="45">whether his intellect is in clarity and purity and brightness,</t>
    <t s="46">or not,</t>
    <t s="47">that these changes can occur in one day,</t>
    <t s="48">from one time in the day to a second time in the day.</t>
    <t s="49">And all this is from the perspective of the matter of vessels,</t>
    <t s="50">for since there is a difference between the vessels</t>
    <t s="51">(the vessel of the brain and likewise the vessels of the other powers)</t>
    <t s="52">of this person and the vessels of another person,</t>
    <t s="53">behold, this also affects the revelation,</t>
    <t s="54">that is,</t>
    <t s="55">as the light of intellect is drawn and revealed from the essence of the soul into the power of the intellect and afterwards into greater revelation in revealed intellect,</t>
    <t s="56">then changes occur in it.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides proofs from gilgul and from writing that the change in revealed powers stems only from the vessels, while the light itself remains concealed and unchanged in the soul's essence.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And he continues to explain</t>
    <t s="1">that the change that occurs in the revelation of the powers is only from the perspective of the vessels,</t>
    <t s="2">and the proof of this is from what is seen in the matter of gilgulim,</t>
    <t s="3">that the soul of a person of intellect,</t>
    <t s="4">the aspect of the speaker,</t>
    <t s="5">is reincarnated in an animal or even in a silent [inanimate] object,</t>
    <t s="6">that is,</t>
    <t s="7">that the essence of the soul with all its powers is reincarnated and exists there,</t>
    <t s="8">and nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="9">no change occurs in the living [animal] and all the more so in the silent [inanimate] object that there should be in them the matter of intellect that belongs to the species of the speaker.</t>
    <t s="10">And the explanation of this,</t>
    <t s="11">since there is no vessel there suitable to receive the light of intellect,</t>
    <t s="12">therefore the light remains in concealment,</t>
    <t s="13">and this is,</t>
    <t s="14">that even though it exists there,</t>
    <t s="15">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="16">it remains in that same manner as it exists in the essence of the soul,</t>
    <t s="17">and it does not come into revelation.</t>
    <t s="18">And behold,</t>
    <t s="19">the above matter is as the light is in such concealment that it does not effect anything.</t>
    <t s="20">And there is another example of this,</t>
    <t s="21">from writing a matter of intellect by means of the fingers of the hand.</t>
    <t s="22">For behold,</t>
    <t s="23">even though the vessel for intellect is the brain in the head,</t>
    <t s="24">behold, we see that when a person writes a matter of intellect with his hand,</t>
    <t s="25">the movement of the fingers must be in a specific manner so that a matter of wisdom and intellect will be revealed in the writing,</t>
    <t s="26">and not a matter that has no wisdom or intellect or an opposite matter.</t>
    <t s="27">And it follows,</t>
    <t s="28">that even though the hand and fingers are not vessels at all for the power of intellect,</t>
    <t s="29">and the proof,</t>
    <t s="30">that as soon as he stops writing, no matter of intellect is discernible in the fingers of the hand,</t>
    <t s="31">and nothing remains in them except the power of movement alone,</t>
    <t s="32">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="33">at the time of writing we see how the matter of intellect is drawn through the fingers of the hand.</t>
    <t s="34">And as it is brought in several discourses</t>
    <t s="35">an example of this even in habit,</t>
    <t s="36">as is seen in the matter of dancing in a way that the movement of the legs is directed to the melodies of the tune,</t>
    <t s="37">that he can direct the beat</t>
    <t s="38">(as the language in the discourse),</t>
    <t s="39">that this matter is drawn from the intellect in the head.</t>
    <t s="40">And nevertheless, this is not in a way that the hand or legs are vessels for the intellect,</t>
    <t s="41">for this matter applies only to the vessel of the brain,</t>
    <t s="42">in which the intellect resides,</t>
    <t s="43">but in the other limbs of the body, the intellect exists in concealment,</t>
    <t s="44">by means of the nerves of the brain that spread throughout all the limbs of the body,</t>
    <t s="45">and through them the concealment of the intellect can effect also in the hand or leg that the writing will be in a way that the intellectual matter is revealed in the letters of the writing,</t>
    <t s="46">and likewise regarding the dancing with the leg.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
